title: committed_calls keeps the newest call rows by git grep path order, which is not strictly chronological
goal: Found by the SP-yzs3bj6f review of BG-4tvqk5tp: committed_calls (_tools/bl_intake.py) keeps the last REPEAT_ROWS_MAX rows in git grep path order; 5 of 130 ops sidecars start before the previous file's newest row, so once the rows pass the budget a late-written sidecar holding old-week rows can evict rows of the latest closed ISO week the repeats detector judges. The rows kept are the newest by their week or timestamp (or only the judged week is read), whatever the sidecars' path order, and the notes still count what was left out.

run: import sys,tempfile,subprocess,os,pathlib;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import bl_intake as b;d=tempfile.mkdtemp();o=pathlib.Path(d,b.STORE_REL,'ops');o.mkdir(parents=True);(o/'a.jsonl').write_text('{event:call.tool,ts:2026-10-01T00:00:00Z,class:new}\n');(o/'b.jsonl').write_text('{event:call.tool,ts:2026-09-01T00:00:00Z,class:old}\n');g=lambda *a:subprocess.run(['git','-c','user.name=t','-c','user.email=t@example.com',*a],cwd=d,capture_output=True);g('init','-q');g('add','.');g('commit','-qm','x');r,over=b.committed_calls(d,budget=1);print(r,over);sys.exit(0 if r and r[0][1]=='new' else 1)
